title: Customer spending
task: Calculate spending per customer. Output customer_id, total_spent; sort by customer_id.
sql: SELECT s.customer_id, SUM(m.price) AS total_spent FROM sales s JOIN menu m USING (product_id) GROUP BY s.customer_id ORDER BY s.customer_id;
steps: Join sales to menu using product_id to attach the unit price.
Sum prices for each customer, including every repeated sale.
Order customer IDs for a deterministic result.
note: Aggregate after joining each sale to its menu price. Preserve repeated sales; they are separate purchases.

title: Distinct visit days
task: Count visit dates for each customer. Output customer_id, visit_days; sort by customer_id.
sql: SELECT customer_id, COUNT(DISTINCT order_date) AS visit_days FROM sales GROUP BY customer_id ORDER BY customer_id;
steps: A sales row is an item, not a visit.
Count distinct order_date values per customer. Multiple items on the same date count as one visit.
note: COUNT(DISTINCT) deduplicates dates within each customer; COUNT(*) would count items.

title: First purchases
task: Find each customer’s earliest purchased dishes. Output customer_id, product_name. Keep distinct dishes tied on the first date; sort by customer_id, product_name. There is no time-of-day or order ID to break same-day ties.
sql: WITH first_dates AS (SELECT customer_id, MIN(order_date) AS first_date FROM sales GROUP BY customer_id) SELECT DISTINCT s.customer_id, m.product_name FROM sales s JOIN first_dates f ON s.customer_id=f.customer_id AND s.order_date=f.first_date JOIN menu m USING (product_id) ORDER BY s.customer_id, m.product_name;
steps: Find the minimum purchase date for each customer.
Join back to all sales on that date, then attach dish names.
Deduplicate dish names, not sales before calculating purchase counts elsewhere.
note: Do not pick one arbitrary same-day purchase with ROW_NUMBER.

title: Bestselling dishes
task: Find the overall bestseller and its purchase count. Output product_name, purchases; include ties, sort product_name.
sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT m.product_name, COUNT(*) AS purchases FROM sales s JOIN menu m USING (product_id) GROUP BY m.product_name) SELECT product_name, purchases FROM counts WHERE purchases=(SELECT MAX(purchases) FROM counts) ORDER BY product_name;
steps: Count sales of each dish across all customers.
Compare each count with the maximum group count.
Keep all tied winners.
note: Aggregate after joining each sale to its menu price. Preserve repeated sales; they are separate purchases.

title: Customer favorites
task: Find each customer’s most ordered dishes. Output customer_id, product_name, purchases. Keep all ties, sorted by customer_id, product_name.
sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT s.customer_id, m.product_name, COUNT(*) AS purchases FROM sales s JOIN menu m USING (product_id) GROUP BY s.customer_id,m.product_name), ranked AS (SELECT *, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY purchases DESC) AS r FROM counts) SELECT customer_id,product_name,purchases FROM ranked WHERE r=1 ORDER BY customer_id,product_name;
steps: Count purchases by both customer and dish.
Rank those counts within each customer.
Keep rank 1, including every tied favorite.
note: Aggregate before ranking so the window processes groups instead of raw sales.

title: First member purchases
task: Find the earliest dishes purchased as a member. Output customer_id, product_name; keep distinct tied dishes and sort by both columns. Convention: the join date counts as membership (order_date >= join_date).
sql: WITH eligible AS (SELECT s.*, MIN(s.order_date) OVER (PARTITION BY s.customer_id) AS first_date FROM sales s JOIN members b USING (customer_id) WHERE s.order_date>=b.join_date) SELECT DISTINCT e.customer_id,m.product_name FROM eligible e JOIN menu m USING (product_id) WHERE e.order_date=e.first_date ORDER BY e.customer_id,m.product_name;
steps: Join members to sales and remove purchases before joining.
Compute the first qualifying date for each member.
Return every distinct dish on that date.
note: Apply membership eligibility before finding the minimum date.

title: Last purchases before joining
task: Find the last pre-membership dishes. Output customer_id, product_name; preserve distinct tied dishes and sort both columns. Pre-membership means order_date < join_date.
sql: WITH eligible AS (SELECT s.*, MAX(s.order_date) OVER (PARTITION BY s.customer_id) AS last_date FROM sales s JOIN members b USING (customer_id) WHERE s.order_date<b.join_date) SELECT DISTINCT e.customer_id,m.product_name FROM eligible e JOIN menu m USING (product_id) WHERE e.order_date=e.last_date ORDER BY e.customer_id,m.product_name;
steps: Filter to dates strictly before the member joined.
Find the latest remaining date within each member.
Retain all distinct dishes on that date.
note: Using <= would incorrectly include joining-day purchases.

title: Pre-membership totals
task: Summarize items and spending before joining. Output customer_id, total_items, total_spent; sort customer_id. Include registered members with no earlier purchases as zero totals; nonmembers are excluded.
sql: SELECT b.customer_id, COUNT(s.product_id) AS total_items, COALESCE(SUM(m.price),0) AS total_spent FROM members b LEFT JOIN sales s ON s.customer_id=b.customer_id AND s.order_date<b.join_date LEFT JOIN menu m ON m.product_id=s.product_id GROUP BY b.customer_id ORDER BY b.customer_id;
steps: Start from members so a member with no earlier sales can still appear.
Put the date condition in the LEFT JOIN; a WHERE filter could discard zero-purchase members.
Count matched items, sum prices, and replace an empty sum with zero.
note: COUNT(*) on a left join would count the unmatched placeholder row.

title: Standard loyalty points
task: Compute each customer’s points: 10 per dollar, doubled for sushi. Output customer_id, points; sort customer_id. This exercise includes every customer and all dates regardless of membership.
sql: SELECT s.customer_id, SUM(m.price*10*CASE WHEN m.product_name='sushi' THEN 2 ELSE 1 END) AS points FROM sales s JOIN menu m USING (product_id) GROUP BY s.customer_id ORDER BY s.customer_id;
steps: Attach price and product name to each sale.
Use CASE for the sushi multiplier; apply it to price times ten.
Sum the points per customer.
note: Aggregate after joining each sale to its menu price. Preserve repeated sales; they are separate purchases.

title: January welcome-week points
task: Compute January points for members A and B. Output customer_id, points; sort customer_id. Use January 1–31, 2021. Exercise convention: pre-join purchases earn standard points; joining day through day 6 earn double points on every dish; sushi stays double outside that window. Multipliers never stack. February purchases are excluded.
sql: SELECT b.customer_id, COALESCE(SUM(m.price*10*CASE WHEN s.order_date BETWEEN b.join_date AND b.join_date+6 THEN 2 WHEN m.product_name='sushi' THEN 2 ELSE 1 END),0) AS points FROM members b LEFT JOIN sales s ON s.customer_id=b.customer_id AND s.order_date>=DATE '2021-01-01' AND s.order_date<DATE '2021-02-01' LEFT JOIN menu m ON m.product_id=s.product_id WHERE b.customer_id IN ('A','B') GROUP BY b.customer_id ORDER BY b.customer_id;
steps: Restrict sales to January before calculating points.
Check the inclusive seven-day welcome window first; otherwise apply the ordinary sushi rule.
Use a single multiplier so welcome-week sushi is double, not quadruple.
This exercise explicitly awards standard points before joining; a policy that excludes those dates gives different totals.
note: Use an exclusive next-month boundary; joining day + 6 is the seventh day.

title: Bonus: membership purchase ledger
task: Build a purchase ledger. Output customer_id, order_date, product_name, price, member. Label eligible member purchases Y and all others N. Preserve duplicate sales; sort customer_id, order_date, product_name.
sql: SELECT s.customer_id,s.order_date,m.product_name,m.price,CASE WHEN s.order_date>=b.join_date THEN 'Y' ELSE 'N' END AS member FROM sales s JOIN menu m USING (product_id) LEFT JOIN members b USING (customer_id) ORDER BY s.customer_id,s.order_date,m.product_name;
steps: Join every sale to its menu entry.
Left join membership records to retain customer C.
CASE marks joining-day and subsequent member purchases Y; NULL membership dates fall into N.
note: Do not add DISTINCT: the ledger must preserve repeated purchases.

title: Bonus: member purchase ranks
task: Extend the ledger with ranking. Output customer_id, order_date, product_name, price, member, ranking. Rank member purchase dates using RANK; same-date purchases tie and create gaps. Pre-membership and nonmember rows have NULL ranking. Sort customer_id, order_date, product_name.
sql: WITH ledger AS (SELECT s.customer_id,s.order_date,m.product_name,m.price,CASE WHEN s.order_date>=b.join_date THEN 'Y' ELSE 'N' END AS member FROM sales s JOIN menu m USING (product_id) LEFT JOIN members b USING (customer_id)) SELECT customer_id,order_date,product_name,price,member,CASE WHEN member='Y' THEN RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id,member ORDER BY order_date) END AS ranking FROM ledger ORDER BY customer_id,order_date,product_name;
steps: Build the membership ledger first.
Partition the ranking by customer and membership flag, so pre-join purchases cannot shift member ranks.
Use RANK for ties and gaps; CASE hides ranks for N rows.
note: RANK and DENSE_RANK agree on some sample rows but differ when tied member dates precede later dates. The edge fixture tests this.
